speaker: jessica
text: Theater chains just bet their whole year on Spider-Man.
visual: Deep-blue full-bleed card; bold white text 'ONE MOVIE. ONE QUARTER.' with a web-red underline sweeping in left-to-right; a date chip flips to 'JULY 31, 2026'

speaker: george
text: Spider-Man: Brand New Day, July 31. Tracking says a $180–190 million opening — biggest of 2026.
visual: Animated horizontal range bar filling from $0 to a $180M–$190M band in web-red; a gray tick at $159.7M labeled 'Toy Story 5 — 2026's current #1' gets overtaken, badge pops: 'BIGGEST OF 2026'

speaker: jessica
visual: The range bar shrinks to a small corner card; a big pulsing '?' in soft blue over the words 'fine... right?'

speaker: george
text: AMC lost $632 million last year. Their own math: every $100M more at the box office adds $18M.
visual: Counter crashes from $0 to -$632.4M in red ('AMC net loss, FY2025 — SEC filing'); then an equation animates: '+$100M industry box office → +$18M AMC EBITDA' with stacking coin blocks per $100M

speaker: jessica
visual: A 'STAKES' meter needle sweeps from LOW to MAX, tinting the frame edge web-red

speaker: george
text: Good news: best first-day presales in five years. Fandango top-ten all-time.
visual: Leaderboard of 2026 first-day pre-sellers (The Odyssey, Mandalorian & Grogu, Project Hail Mary); 'Brand New Day' row slides to #1 in red; stamp: 'FANDANGO TOP-10 ALL-TIME' + 'best first day since 2021'

speaker: jessica
visual: Leaderboard freezes mid-shine; brief red glitch/scratch effect; the word 'CATCH:' types out

speaker: george
text: Zero US IMAX screens opening weekend — Nolan's Odyssey locked them all.
visual: Grid of screen icons labeled IMAX; each fills with 'ODYSSEY' in blue one by one; a counter reads 'BRAND NEW DAY US IMAX SCREENS: 0'; footnote chip: 'exclusive multi-week window'

speaker: jessica
visual: Two arrows tug in opposite directions over a blank axis labeled 'opening weekend forecast', gap between them flashing '~$50–60M apart'

speaker: george
text: Boxoffice Pro says $230–250 million. The comp is No Way Home's $260M — only nine films ever opened above $200M.
visual: Dual range bars: Deadline $180–190M (blue) vs Boxoffice Pro $230–250M (red); dashed line drops in at $260.1M labeled 'No Way Home, 2021'; annotation fades up: 'only 9 films ever opened above $200M domestic'

speaker: jessica
visual: The forecast chart dims to grayscale; a red down-arrow traces below the $180M band; screen edge darkens

speaker: george
text: AMC: four billion in debt, stock under two bucks. This isn't a premiere — it's the whole bet.
visual: Split card: towering '$4B DEBT' bar in blue beside a tiny stock ticker '$1.94 ▼46% off 52-wk high'; final stamp slams in web-red on deep blue: 'THE SPIDER-MAN BET — JULY 31', echoing the opening title card
